title: Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan Delivers 2.89 Lakh Pucca Houses Worth ₹3,473 Crore to Rajasthan Under PMAY-G
subtitle:
340.59 Crore Approved for Agricultural Development and PM-RKVY; Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan Hands Over Sanction Letter to CM Shri Bhajan Lal Sharma
29.13 Lakh New Beneficiaries Surveyed Under PMAY-G; More Houses to be Sanctioned After Physical Verification: Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan
Major PMAY-G Eligibility Reforms: Two-Wheeler Owners, Women Earning Up to ₹15,000 and Small Farmers Now Eligible for Housing Support
No Woman Should Remain Poor: Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan Doubles Rajasthan’s Lakhpati Didi Target to 32 Lakh
Viksit Bharat-G RAM G Yojana: ₹12,000 Crore Target for Rajasthan; Panchayats to Drive Development with Annual Goal of ₹80 Lakh Each
Urea at ₹266 a Bag for Farmers Despite ₹3,000 Cost: Government Continues to Bear the Burden, Says Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan
Tougher Laws Against Fake Pesticides and Substandard Seeds: New Pesticide and Seed Legislation to be Introduced in Parliament, Says Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan
body_text:
Union Minister for Agriculture & Farmers Welfare and Rural Development Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan, during his visit to Rajasthan today, participated in the state-level program of the Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana-Gramin in Baran along with Chief Minister Shri Bhajanlal Sharma. On the occasion, Shri Chouhan handed over to the Chief Minister the approval letter for 2,89,355 houses under PMAY-G, involving a project outlay of ₹3,473 crore. He also handed over an approval letter for ₹340.59 crore under agricultural development initiatives and the Pradhan Mantri Rashtriya Krishi Vikas Yojana. The program was attended by Members of Parliament, MLAs, ministers in charge, and a large number of local residents.
PM’s Commitment to Pucca Houses for the Poor Being Fulfilled
Addressing the gathering, Union Minister Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan said that Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi’s commitment to providing pucca houses to poor families in Rajasthan is being fulfilled. “Today, approval is being given for 2,89,355 houses at a cost of ₹3,473 crore and this gift is being dedicated to Rajasthan. It will bring a positive transformation in the lives of families who have so far been living in kutcha houses,” he said. He added that ₹340.59 crore under various agriculture-related schemes has also been released for the development of the state.
Survey Completed for 29.13 Lakh New Beneficiaries
Shri Chouhan informed that a survey of 29,13,749 new beneficiaries has been completed. After physical verification, houses will also be sanctioned for the remaining eligible beneficiaries. He directed that transparent beneficiary lists be displayed at the district and panchayat levels, objections be heard, and wrongful exclusion of eligible beneficiaries be prevented so that deserving families do not lose their benefits due to errors.
Three Major Changes in Eligibility Rules
Shri Chouhan announced three major changes in the eligibility criteria for housing assistance. Families owning a two-wheeler will now also be eligible for a pucca house, removing the earlier restriction. Women earning up to ₹15,000 per month will also be eligible for the benefit. The earlier income ceiling was ₹10,000 per month. Small farmers owning up to 5 acres of unirrigated land or 2.5 acres of irrigated land will also be eligible for housing assistance.
Women’s Empowerment and Lakhpati Didi Mission
The Union Minister said that women’s empowerment is one of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi’s key priorities. He announced that 16 lakh women in Rajasthan have so far become Lakhpati Didis, and the target will now be doubled to 32 lakh Lakhpati Didis. Shri Chouhan further said that ₹13,400 crore has so far been disbursed to women through various banks to support their entrepreneurial activities.
Viksit Bharat-G RAM G Yojana for Rural Development
Referring to the newly introduced Viksit Bharat-G RAM G Yojana, Shri Chouhan said that Rajasthan has been given a target of ₹12,000 crore in investment over the next nine months. He said the impact of the initiative would reach every gram panchayat, with a target of providing approximately ₹80 lakh annually to each panchayat. The Union Minister made it clear that development priorities in villages would not be decided in Delhi or Jaipur. “The people themselves will decide development plans at the panchayat level,” he said.
Ensuring Fertiliser Availability and Protecting Farmers from High Costs
On the availability of urea, Shri Chouhan said the government was ensuring that farmers were not burdened by international prices. He said that although a bag of urea costs around ₹3,000, arrangements have been made to ensure that farmers receive it for only ₹266. He also assured farmers of strict action against black marketing of fertilisers and other agricultural inputs.
Strict Action Against Fake Agricultural Inputs
Shri Chouhan said that the existing legal framework is not adequate to deal with the menace of fake pesticides and substandard seeds. He announced that stronger legislation relating to pesticides and seeds would be brought in the next session of Parliament, with provisions for stringent punishment for those involved in such malpractice and stronger protection for farmers.
Agriculture Roadmap for the Kota-Jhalawar Region
Shri Chouhan said that he would work with scientists and local farmers to prepare a comprehensive agricultural roadmap for the Kota-Jhalawar region. The roadmap, he said, would focus on the entire value chain, including new crops, processing, marketing and exports, with the objective of increasing farmers’ incomes from the farm gate to global markets.
Call for Service and Collective Participation
The Union Minister praised the leadership of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi and the state government and called upon citizens to contribute to social causes, including serving society, planting trees, educating daughters and promoting a drug-free society. He also administered a pledge to those present and called upon everyone to work together towards building a Viksit Rajasthan and Viksit Gaon.
Vande Mataram is a symbol of India’s freedom struggle, sacrifice and patriotism: Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan
In his address, Union Minister Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan said that Vande Mataram is a symbol of India’s freedom struggle, sacrifice and patriotism, and that respecting it is the duty of every Indian.

enrichment.summary: Union Minister Shivraj Singh Chouhan, during a visit to Baran, Rajasthan, handed Chief Minister Bhajan Lal Sharma a sanction letter for 2.89 lakh houses worth ₹3,473 crore under PMAY-Gramin, along with ₹340.59 crore for agricultural development and PM-RKVY. He announced three major PMAY-G eligibility reforms — two-wheeler owners are now eligible, the income ceiling for eligible women was raised from ₹10,000 to ₹15,000/month, and small farmers with up to 5 acres unirrigated/2.5 acres irrigated land now qualify. He also announced doubling of Rajasthan's Lakhpati Didi target to 32 lakh, a ₹12,000 crore target for the state under the new Viksit Bharat-G RAM G Yojana, and plans for tougher pesticide and seed legislation in the next Parliament session.
enrichment.context:
PMAY-Gramin, launched in 2016, aims to provide pucca houses with basic amenities to rural poor households, with eligibility earlier determined via the Socio-Economic Caste Census (SECC) and subsequent Awaas+ surveys. Periodic revisions to eligibility criteria — such as relaxing restrictions tied to asset ownership (two-wheelers, landholding size) and raising income thresholds for women beneficiaries — reflect the government's effort to widen coverage to previously excluded near-poor households, especially as inflation erodes the value of older income caps. Such changes matter for UPSC aspirants tracking welfare scheme design and targeting mechanisms under GS Paper 2.

The announcement of the 'Viksit Bharat-G RAM G Yojana' appears to be a new rural development initiative emphasizing panchayat-led, decentralized planning, resonating with the 73rd Constitutional Amendment's vision of Gram Panchayats as units of local self-governance and planning. The mention of upcoming pesticide and seed legislation reflects long-standing concerns about spurious agricultural inputs harming farmer incomes, an issue often raised in agricultural policy debates. The Lakhpati Didi scheme, tied to the Deendayal Antyodaya Yojana-National Rural Livelihoods Mission (DAY-NRLM), aims to make women in Self-Help Groups earn over ₹1 lakh annually, and its target-doubling signals expanded women's economic empowerment efforts.

options: Small farmers owning up to 5 acres of unirrigated land or 2.5 acres of irrigated land
prelims_questions.explanation: The release states that small farmers owning up to 5 acres of unirrigated or 2.5 acres of irrigated land are now eligible for PMAY-G housing assistance, along with two-wheeler owners and women earning up to ₹15,000/month.

prelims_questions.question: The 'Lakhpati Didi' initiative, whose target for Rajasthan was doubled to 32 lakh as per this release, is associated with which broader rural livelihoods programme?
options: Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act (MGNREGA)
Deendayal Antyodaya Yojana-National Rural Livelihoods Mission (DAY-NRLM)
prelims_questions.explanation: Lakhpati Didi is a scheme under DAY-NRLM aimed at enabling women in Self-Help Groups to earn a sustainable annual household income of over ₹1 lakh.

mains_questions.question: Discuss the significance of periodically revising eligibility criteria under welfare housing schemes like PMAY-Gramin. What challenges arise in balancing wider coverage with fiscal sustainability and targeting accuracy?

Examine the role of decentralized, panchayat-led planning in rural development schemes. How can initiatives that empower Gram Panchayats to decide local development priorities strengthen the spirit of the 73rd Constitutional Amendment?

study_notes.reason: The release carries a testable factual core (PMAY-G eligibility criteria revisions, scheme numbers) alongside genuine analytical value on welfare scheme targeting design and rural decentralised planning, making it dual-use rather than skewed to one side.

prelims.point: PMAY-Gramin (Pradhan Mantri Awaas Yojana-Gramin) - eligibility now extended to two-wheeler owning families, removing an earlier exclusion criterion
prelims.why_important: Asset-ownership exclusion criteria under PMAY-G (mobile phones, two-wheelers, refrigerators etc.) are a classic UPSC testing point on scheme eligibility design.

prelims.point: PMAY-G income ceiling for eligible women beneficiaries raised from ₹10,000/month to ₹15,000/month
prelims.why_important: Specific numeric thresholds in welfare schemes are a common statement-based prelims target.

prelims.point: PMAY-G land-holding eligibility raised to 5 acres unirrigated or 2.5 acres irrigated land for small farmers
prelims.why_important: Distinguishing irrigated vs unirrigated land thresholds is the kind of nuanced detail UPSC uses to test careful reading.

prelims.point: Lakhpati Didi scheme is linked to DAY-NRLM and targets women in Self-Help Groups earning over ₹1 lakh annually
prelims.why_important: Aspirants must know Lakhpati Didi's parent umbrella scheme (DAY-NRLM) and its income-based definition of success.

prelims.point: 'Viksit Bharat-G RAM G Yojana' announced as a new panchayat-level rural development investment scheme
prelims.why_important: New scheme names are frequently tested for objectives, implementing level, and target beneficiaries.

mains.point: Periodic relaxation of PMAY-G eligibility criteria (asset ownership, income ceilings, landholding limits) reflects efforts to correct exclusion errors in welfare targeting as inflation and asset penetration change over time
mains.theme: Welfare scheme targeting and exclusion errors
mains.analytical_use: Useful for questions on challenges in identifying beneficiaries for welfare schemes and how eligibility criteria must be periodically revised to prevent wrongful exclusion.

mains.point: Directive for transparent, publicly displayed beneficiary lists at district/panchayat level to address wrongful exclusion of eligible households
mains.theme: Transparency and accountability in scheme implementation
mains.analytical_use: Supports answers on grievance redress mechanisms and social audit practices in rural welfare delivery.

mains.point: Viksit Bharat-G RAM G Yojana's design channels funds directly to gram panchayats for locally-decided development priorities
mains.analytical_use: Can be used to discuss strengthening of the 73rd Amendment's vision of panchayats as planning units and challenges of fiscal decentralisation.

mains.point: Government acknowledges inadequacy of existing legal framework against fake pesticides and substandard seeds, necessitating new legislation
mains.theme: Agricultural input regulation and farmer protection
mains.analytical_use: Relevant for questions on ensuring quality of agricultural inputs and protecting farmer incomes from spurious products.

mains.point: Subsidised urea pricing (farmers pay ₹266 against actual cost of ~₹3,000) illustrates continued fertiliser subsidy burden on the exchequer
mains.theme: Fertiliser subsidy and input cost management
mains.analytical_use: Useful for evaluating the fiscal sustainability and efficiency of input subsidies versus direct income support in agriculture.
